quote: I am still in California right now. I won't be back till next week.
stewart_read: Customer discloses he's out of state at the time of the call, which the rep never explicitly reconciles until scheduling — it resurfaces at 05:42 when the rep asks if he's out of town all week, but the intervening logistics (is he home for the appointment window) were not locked down until late in the call.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep simply forgot the detail and asked again later out of necessity, not strategy.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to note travel/availability constraints immediately and confirm the appointment window against them early, rather than re-discovering the constraint near the end of the call.

quote: I don't know. I just bought the house.
stewart_read: This is the moment the schema's bill-amount capture should happen, but the customer has no bill history, creating a genuine data gap rather than a stall.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep could have pivoted to asking what the previous owner's utility costs looked like on record, or asked the customer's expectation of a typical bill for a house this size, to still create an anchor.
coaching_implication: Even without a bill, the rep could ask 'what would you guess a typical bill runs for a two-story home like this' to keep the emotional anchor alive instead of dropping straight to a technical workaround.

quote: I can tell you what my kilowatt usage is right now.
stewart_read: The rep accepts a live kWh reading as sufficient qualification data but never converts it into a forward-pulling hook — no follow-up like 'that's a solid number to build a design around' or tying it to potential savings once he's home. The number is filed, not leveraged.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep may have simply been in verify-checklist mode and treated this as a box to check, not a moment to build on.
coaching_implication: Train the rep to reflect any usage or bill number back to the customer with a forward-looking hook, even when the number is unconventional (a live reading instead of a monthly bill).

stewart_read: Rep reads back a phone number to confirm where to send the text, which is a minor logistics moment but shows the rep using his own line for bill collection rather than a company-anchored channel.
coaching_implication: Not a priority coaching item, but worth a note if the floor is standardizing on a non-personal number for bill/photo collection per the schema's automated bill capture roadmap.

quote: Okay. Let me just go talk to him, and then I think we'll we'll be good to go. Okay?
stewart_read: Rep places the customer on hold to consult a supervisor because the new-homeowner-no-bill-history scenario isn't a standard script path, and needs sign-off that a live usage reading is an acceptable substitute for a bill.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: could also read as the rep being unsure of policy rather than following a known non-standard-scenario protocol.
coaching_implication: If this substitution is common (new homeowners without bill history), the manager should confirm with leadership whether this is now a standard accepted path so future reps don't need a hold to resolve it.

quote: So you just got it. Let me tell him you just got it the house, like, last month, this last two months.
stewart_read: Rep misstates the purchase timing to relay to the supervisor (guessing 'last month, this last two months') before the customer corrects him with the exact close date, showing the rep hadn't retained the detail accurately before escalating it.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive slip in the moment rather than a systemic issue — the customer immediately corrects it and the rep moves on without consequence to the booking.
coaching_implication: Minor, but worth flagging: when relaying customer facts to a supervisor or closer, restate the customer's own words rather than approximating, since inaccurate relay can create confusion downstream.

quote: Alright. I'll also just let you know, it has to be on the rear of the house. It cannot be seen from the street.
stewart_read: Customer raises an HOA-driven placement constraint at the very end of the call; the rep defers it entirely to the specialist without capturing any detail (e.g., which HOA rules, whether there's documentation) for the handoff.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: correctly recognizing this is closer-tier technical/design content and using the escape hatch is schema-aligned setter behavior.
coaching_implication: The deferral itself is correct scope discipline, but the rep should have logged this constraint clearly in the notes for the closer rather than letting it pass with only 'that's fine, you'll talk to the specialist.'

quote: Oh, I was gonna ask about that.
stewart_read: Rep begins to ask about HOA status reactively after the customer's own line seems to have already answered it, showing the rep working from a mental checklist rather than a fully natural conversational flow.
coaching_implication: Minor pacing note — not a priority, but indicates the rep is checklist-driven rather than weaving verify items conversationally per coaching_philosophy on Verify.
